purpose: Captopril is used to treat high blood pressure, which helps lower your risk of heart attack and stroke. It is also used to help your heart pump more effectively if you have heart failure or have had a heart attack. In some cases, it is used to protect the kidneys in people with diabetes.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called angiotensin II that tightens your blood vessels and raises your blood pressure. Captopril blocks the enzyme that produces this chemical, so your blood vessels relax and widen. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down to a healthier level.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a dry, persistent cough that some people find bothersome. You may also notice dizziness, especially when you stand up quickly, as well as tiredness or a mild skin rash. Some people experience a change in taste or an upset stomach.
warnings: This medication should NEVER be taken during pregnancy, as it can seriously harm or even cause the death of an unborn baby — tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. It can sometimes cause dangerously high potassium levels, so avoid extra potassium supplements or salt substitutes unless your doctor approves. Rarely, it can cause severe swelling of the face, lips, or throat (called angioedema) — if this happens, seek emergency help immediately. Have your kidney function and blood potassium checked regularly while on this medication.
typical_dosing: For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose is 12.5 mg to 25 mg taken two to three times a day, and your doctor may increase it gradually up to 150 mg per day. Captopril is best taken on an empty stomach, about one hour before meals, since food can reduce how well it is absorbed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
